earlier_scan.source_named: Only wordlists exist (Smits & Voorhoeve 1992; Galis 1955); GlottologGlottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist. No grammar or phonology of Meoswar located.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Roswar (Saref)', Provinsi Papua Barat (entry idb 673; = Bahasa dan Peta Bahasa di Indonesia). Jakarta: Kemendikdasmen (online, accessed 2026-09-20).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content: location, neighbouring languages (Wandamen, Wamesa) and dialectometric distances only ('isolek Roswar merupakan bahasa tersendiri.. dengan bahasa Ron 92,67%, bahasa Beser 96%, dan bahasa Sumuri 98,67%'). Implies Badan Bahasa holds an unpublished 200-item Roswar wordlist - wordlist-only.

sources.citation: Bach, Xavier C. A. 2021. 'Alienable' possession in Biakic. Transactions of the Philological Society 119(3): 330–345. doi:10.1111/1467-968X.12221 (open-access copy from Oxford ORA).
sources.note: Only modern first-hand Meoswar data (author's 2015 fieldwork at CELD Manokwari, consultants Luter Rumberpro, Hengky Semuai, Ansomi Wandau). Morphosyntax of possession only; the sole phonological remarks are PMP *t > k in Biak/Roon/Meoswar and '/r/ is realized [d] after a nasal' (fn. 5, p. 336). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Yulianti, Santy & Winci Firdaus. 2020. Keterancaman Bahasa Roswar: Analisis Daya Hidup Bahasa. Ranah: Jurnal Kajian Bahasa 9(2): 358–373.
sources.note: Gold-OA Badan Bahasa vitality study of 'bahasa Roswar' (Distrik Roswar, Teluk Wondama); needed only to settle whether Roswar = Meoswar and to see whether Badan Bahasa holds a Roswar wordlist/phonology (their Peta Bahasa entry 'Roswar or Saref').

sources.citation: Kamholz, David C. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera–West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley.
sources.note: Comparative work; Meoswar data come only from Anceaux (n.d.) notebook and Smits & Voorhoeve (1992b) wordlists ('There are few data available for Meoswar', ch. 3). §5.4 proposes Proto-SHWNG penultimate stress and cites penultimate stress as the default for Buli, Sawai, Taba, Ambai, Wandamen, Waropen, Warembori — Meoswar is NOT named; no Meoswar stress statement.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (comp.). Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: 'Meoswar, West Papua, Indonesia'. Two data sets: (a) Theodore & Jean Henning, Summer Institute of Linguistics, Irian Jaya, 20 August 1993; (b) Marcel de Jong, GKI-TP Papua, 21 February 2015. Leipzig: MPI-EVA (web page, last data 2015).
sources.note: No phonology content: numerals 1-2000 in plain orthography without stress or tone marks; comments only on the vigesimal system and endangerment. Wordlist-only data, no statement. Lead: the Hennings (SIL, Wandamen programme) collected Meoswar data in 1993, so an unpublished SIL Irian Jaya wordlist/survey sheet may exist.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J. C. 1961. The linguistic situation in the islands of Yapen, Kurudu, Nau and Miosnum, New Guinea. Verhandelingen KITLV 35. The Hague: Nijhoff.
sources.note: Bach 2021 says Anceaux (1961) analyses Meoswar inalienable possession, so it contains some Meoswar data; its comparative Cenderawasih Bay section may note stress. Brill/OAPEN download attempts could not be reached by automated download.
Alternative names War, Meoswar; only reference Kamholz 2014 p.138 (subclassification) and Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment). No descriptive reference.

sources.citation: Xavier Bach, personal research page 'SHWNG languages' (sites.google.com/view/xavierbach).
sources.note: Lists 2015 fieldwork on Biak, Meoswar, Kurudu; publications: Bach 2021 (possession), in-progress 'Gender in Biakic' and Biak prepositions poster. No Meoswar phonology announced.

sources.citation: Bach, Xavier C. A. — unpublished Meoswar field materials (2015, CELD Universitas Papua, Manokwari; consultants L. Rumberpro, H. Semuai, A. Wandau), and in-progress 'Gender in Biakic' chapter.
